title: Inverting Op-Amp: Why the Gain Is a Ratio of Resistors
topic: Inverting amplifier — V_in through R1 into the V- node, feedback through Rf to the output; negative feedback drives V- to the V+ (ground) voltage so V- is a virtual ground; the same current through R1 and Rf gives V_out = -(Rf/R1) · V_in

beats.narration: An op-amp with one resistor in, one resistor in the feedback — what does that do to a signal?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
Two resistors, one op-amp — where does V_out land?

beats.narration: Send V in through R one into the inverting input. Tie a feedback resistor R f from the output back to the same node. The non-inverting input is grounded.

elements.content: Op-amp triangle body, point right
Minus on V- input, plus on V+ input
R1 zigzag, horizontal, from V_in to V- node
V_in label at left, R1 label above zigzag
Feedback loop from output up, left, down to V- node, Rf zigzag along the top
Rf label above feedback zigzag
V+ tied to ground (ground triangle below)
Output wire to the right with V_out label

beats.narration: The op-amp drives its output until V minus equals V plus. V plus sits at ground, so V minus is forced to zero volts — a virtual ground that the wire never actually touches.

elements.content: Same diagram but reduced opacity; V- node highlighted with a pulsing ring
V- = 0 V (virtual ground) annotation pointing at the V- node
negative feedback locks V- to V+ — and V+ is ground

beats.narration: The same current flows through R one and R f, so V out equals minus R f over R one times V in. Push V in up by one volt, output drops by R f over R one volts.

elements.content: I = V_in / R1
V_out = -I · Rf
V_out = -(Rf/R1) · V_in
the gain is just the ratio of two resistors

beats.narration: Sweep V in as a slow sine. V out is the same sine, flipped upside down and scaled by the resistor ratio.

elements.content: Time-axis scope, two horizontal lanes — V_in on top, V_out on bottom
V_in sine traces left-to-right, modest amplitude
V_out sine traces synchronously, inverted and larger amplitude
Vertical time cursor sweeps with the traces

beats.narration: Negative feedback locks the inverting input to ground. The gain is the resistor ratio, and the sign is flipped.

elements.content: V_out = -(Rf/R1) · V_in
two resistors set the gain. the minus sign is the inversion.
